id.description: Unique identifier for the Issue entity.

description.description: A detailed description of the solution.

firestore.reasoning:
The Firestore data structure is designed to ensure security, scalability, and ease of debugging, following the principles of Authorization Independence, Clarity of Intent, DBAC, and QAPs. We are employing Structural Segregation for homogeneous security postures.  Since WebsiteReports are private to a user, we leverage path-based ownership.  Issues are also private to a user, and related to a specific WebsiteReport, so we nest issues under WebsiteReports under users.  Solutions are globally available to all users, and are not private, so they are in their own collection at the top level. Thus, to reduce storage costs, the solution is included in the issue documents. 

Authorization Independence is achieved through path-based ownership: access to website reports and issues is determined directly by the user ID in the path (`/users/{userId}/websiteReports/{websiteReportId}` and `/users/{userId}/websiteReports/{websiteReportId}/issues/{issueId}`). This avoids the need for `get()` calls in security rules, enabling atomic operations.

QAPs are supported by structural segregation: each collection has a clear security posture based on its path. Listing website reports and issues is secure because access is controlled by the user ID in the path, ensuring that only the owner can access their data.  Solutions are global and do not contain any user data, so listing them is also straightforward.
